Put $K=\mathbb Q(q)$, $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, $p=q+q^{-1}$ and $h=q^2+q^{-2}$. For $k\ge0$ set

$$n_{2k}=8k+2,\qquad n_{2k+1}=8k+4,\qquad \ell_{2k}=2,\qquad\ell_{2k+1}=4,\qquad r_j=\ell_j-1,$$

and set $p_j=p$ for even $j$ and $p_j=h$ for odd $j$. Let $u_{j,a}=F^{(a)}u_{j,0}$, $0\le a\le n_j$, be the divided basis of the highest string $V(n_j)$, of weight $n_j-2a$. On the algebraic module $M=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}V(n_j)$ define

$$T_j u_{j,t\ell_j}=(-1)^t u_{j+1,r_j+t\ell_j}\quad(0\le t\le n_j/\ell_j),$$

and define $T_j$ to be zero on all other divided basis vectors. Put $S=\sum_jT_j/p_j$, $C=1+S$, and $b_{j,a}=C u_{j,a}$.

Then $S^2=0$ and $C^{-1}=1-S$; these are finite-column algebraic operators. The homogeneous basis $B=\{b_{j,a}\}$ has a free $U_A$-stable integral span, its standard compatible bar fixes $B$, and its regular zero and infinity charts and crystal residues are those of the standard direct sum of divided strings. Thus it is an actual four-axiom based integrable finite-Cartan-type module, with a balanced integral triple and no choice assumption.

For every $J\ge0$, the finite version $M^{(J)}=\bigoplus_{0\le j\le J}V(n_j)$, with shears only for $j<J$, has the same properties. For every $a\in U_A$ the raw-coordinate action is $C^{-1}aC=a+[a,S]-SaS$; its column at a raw basis vector of index $j$ is supported at summand indices at most $j+2$. That column agrees with the finite version whenever $J\ge j+2$.

The raw seed $b_{0,0}\otimes b_{0,2}$ in two copies has total weight zero and factor weights $2,-2$. Both factors are deformed: $b_{0,0}=u_{0,0}+u_{1,1}/p$ and $b_{0,2}=u_{0,2}-u_{1,3}/p$. This statement constructs the modules and finite versions; it does not assert infinite tensor correction supports.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Let $i\in I$ and let $T_{i,c,t}$ be the toral quantum binomials of
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]
($i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$, $t\ge0$, $T_{i,c,0}=1$), inside the Drinfeld–Jimbo
algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]
with $U_A$ and its parts $U_A^-,U_A^0,U_A^+$ as in that definition. Write
$E=E_i$, $F=F_i$, $E^{(a)}=E_i^{(a)}$, $F^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}$ for the divided
powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] and put
$q=q_i$ inside the displayed formulas.

(i) **Divided-power multiplication.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E^{(a)}E^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iE^{(a+b)},\qquad F^{(a)}F^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iF^{(a+b)}.$$

(ii) **Toral recursion and commutation.** For $t\ge1$,
$$T_{i,c,t}=\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-t+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+t-1}}{q_i^{\,t}-q_i^{\,-t}}\,T_{i,c,t-1}.$$
Each $T_{i,c,t}$ is a Laurent polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in
$\mathbb Q(q)$; the toral elements commute with one another and with all $K_h$.
For all $i,j$ and all $m\in\mathbb Z$ one has
$K_i^{\,m}T_{j,c,t}=T_{j,c,t}K_i^{\,m}$ if $i\ne j$, while
$E_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-2,t}E_i$, $E_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-a_{ij},t}E_j$,
$F_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+2,t}F_i$, $F_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+a_{ij},t}F_j$ for all $j$.
In particular $E_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0E_i$, $F_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0F_i$,
$T_{i,c,t}E_i=E_iT_{i,c+2,t}\in E_iU_A^0$ and
$T_{i,c,t}F_i=F_iT_{i,c-2,t}\in F_iU_A^0$: the toral factor can be moved to the
middle at the cost of a shift of the binomial index.

(iii) **Reordering identity.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}=\sum_{t=0}^{\min(a,b)}F_i^{(b-t)}\,T_{i,\,2t-a-b,\,t}\,E_i^{(a-t)},$$
with every coefficient a toral quantum binomial in $U_A^0$. In particular
$E_iF_i-F_iE_i=T_{i,0,1}$ and
$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(a)}=\sum_{t=0}^{a}F_i^{(a-t)}T_{i,2t-2a,t}E_i^{(a-t)}$.
For $i\ne j$, $E_i^{(a)}$ and $F_j^{(b)}$ commute; the same-half divided powers
$E_i^{(a)},E_j^{(b)}$ (and likewise $F_i^{(a)},F_j^{(b)}$) commute whenever
$a_{ij}=0$, and for $a_{ij}\ne0$ no commutation is asserted.

(iv) **Triangular spanning.** Every element of $U_A$ is an $A$-linear
combination of products $b_-u\,b_+$ with $b_-\in U_A^-$, $u\in U_A^0$ and
$b_+\in U_A^+$; equivalently $U_A=U_A^-U_A^0U_A^+$ as an $A$-module. No
independence of the spanning family is asserted.

In the same positive-first/negative-second completion $\widehat C$ of [[def-root-height-completion-for-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiners]], let $\Theta=\sum_\nu\Theta_\nu$ be the unique normalized bar-coproduct intertwiner of [[thm-the-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiner-exists-and-is-unique]]. Then:

(i) $\Theta^{-1}=\overline\Theta=(\psi\otimes\psi)(\Theta)$, the inverse being taken in the root-height convolution algebra of $\widehat C$ and not switching the positive and negative tensor order;

(ii) for every $\nu$ the exact threefold identities hold:
$$(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{23}(1\otimes K_{-\eta}\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{13},$$
$$(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{12}(1\otimes K_\eta\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{13},$$
with subscripts denoting tensor positions and $\Theta_{\nu'}=0$ when $\nu'\notin Q_+$;

(iii) the two normalized tensor-bar compositions satisfy the field cocycle identity
$$((\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Theta)\Theta_{12}=((\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Theta)\Theta_{23},$$
coefficientwise in the transported source completion and on every vector for which the iterated actions are finite;

(iv) the bar-coproduct counterpart needed for the cocycle is
$$(\mathrm{id}\otimes\overline\Delta)\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{13}(1\otimes K_{-\gamma}\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{12}.$$

Removing the normalization $\Theta_0=1$ permits arbitrary scalar multiples of the same linear intertwiner equation, so normalization is essential for uniqueness; no integrality of coefficients and no uncontrolled infinite evaluation is asserted.

phases.claim: **A uniformly bounded set of positions.** Write an ordinary weight-zero tensor vector as $u_{j,a}\otimes u_{l,n_l-d}$; then $n_j-n_l=2(a-d)$. The seed has $a=d=0$. Both $C$ and $C^{-1}$ preserve $a\le3$ and $d\le3$: on an even link the only eligible positions or endpoint distances in this range are $0,2$, which become $1,3$; on an odd link only $0$ is eligible and it becomes $3$. In endpoint distances the same assertion follows from $n_j\equiv0\pmod{\ell_j}$ and $n_{j+1}=n_j+2(\ell_j-1)$. Every term of $\Theta$ lowers both $a$ and $d$. Thus the raw bar and the correction induction preserve these bounds. Nonadjacent string lengths differ by at least $8$, whereas $|2(a-d)|\le6$, so only equal or adjacent constituent indices occur.

phases.claim: **Parity and the bounded rational states.** Put $\delta_j=\deg_q p_j\pmod2$ and define $\tau_0=0$, $\tau_{j+1}=\tau_j+j+\delta_j\pmod2$. Assign tuple $(j,a,l,n_l-d)$ the parity $\epsilon=a(1+j+l)+\tau_j+\tau_l+jl\pmod2$. Its coefficient in every vector under consideration contains only powers of $q$ of that parity. Indeed $n_j/2\equiv j+1\pmod2$; a first shear has even source position and a second shear has even source position $n_l-d$, hence $a\equiv j+l\pmod2$ in the latter case. In both cases the change of $\epsilon$ is $\delta_j$ or $\delta_l$, exactly the parity of the shear coefficient. A term of $\Theta$ with index $r$ has coefficient parity $r(1+j+l)$, exactly the change from $a$ to $a-r$. The seed has parity zero, positive Laurent extraction preserves parity, and the $D$ coefficients have parity $t(1+j+l)$. In particular diagonal $z_{j,j,a}$ has parity $j+a$. A bar-fixed Laurent polynomial is a polynomial in $p=q+q^{-1}$, by pairing its opposite exponents and the recurrence $q^s+q^{-s}=p(q^{s-1}+q^{1-s})-(q^{s-2}+q^{2-s})$. Multiplying $z$ by its bar-fixed denominator therefore gives a polynomial in $p$; zero residue at both ends bounds its degree strictly below that of the denominator. Thus on an odd diagonal $z_3=c_3/p^2,z_2=A_2/p,z_1=c_1/p^2,z_0=A_0/p$; on an even diagonal $z_3=up/h^2+vp/h$, and initially $z_2,z_0$ have the form $A/h+B/h^2$, while $z_1$ has the form $Ap/h+Bp/h^2$. The constants may be treated over $\mathbb Q$.

**The scalar calculations used below.** On a diagonal of length $m$ write $H_{a,t}=q^{t(m-a+t)}\binom{m-a+t}{t}_q$; this is the coefficient from $D_a$ to first position $a-t$. All following evaluations follow by substituting in $[s]=(q^s-q^{-s})/(q-q^{-1})$ and $\binom Nt_q=\prod_{v=0}^{t-1}[N-v]/[t-v]$. Modulo $h$, one has $p^2=2$, $q^4=-1$, $[8s]/h=-2sp$. For $m=8k+10$ these give $H_{3,1}/h=-2(k+1)p$, $H_{2,2}=-1$, $H_{1,1}=q^2p$, $H_{3,3}/h=2(k+1)q^2p$, and $H_{3,2}$ is divisible by $h$. For $m=8k+4$, all endpoint coefficients $H_{a,a}$ with $1\le a\le3$ vanish modulo $h$. Modulo $p$, one has $q^2=-1$; for $m=8k+4$ the evaluations are $H_{3,1}/p=-(4k+1)$, $H_{3,2}=4k+1$, $H_{1,1}/p=-(4k+2)$, $H_{2,2}=4k+2$, and $H_{3,3}/p=-(4k+2)(4k+1)$. For $m=8k+2$ one has $H_{2,2}=4k+1$. Quotients here are taken only when the numerator is divisible by the indicated denominator, and evaluations are in $\mathbb Q[q,q^{-1}]/(q^4+1)$ or $\mathbb Q[q,q^{-1}]/(q^2+1)$ understood as the corresponding residue fields.

**Base odd diagonal.** For $j=1$, $m=4$, the first-weight bound excludes positions $2,3$, so only $z_1=c/p^2,z_0=A/p$ occur. The double pole in the ordinary component at position $1$ comes only from shearing both seed factors; its sign is negative, hence $c=-1$. The ordinary endpoint has no incoming first shear and no admissible backward mixed tensor with first position $0$, so it equals its Laurent integral raw coefficient. Since $H_{1,1}/p=-2$ modulo $p$, cancellation of its simple pole forces $A=2c=-2$. Thus the odd scalar starts at $c_0=-1$, with endpoint residue $-2/p=-p=q^3-q$ modulo $h$.

**Odd to even: the double pole.** Suppose the odd diagonal $j=2k+1$, $m=8k+4$, has $z_3=z_1=c/p^2$, $z_2=(4k+1)c/p$ and $z_0=(4k+2)c/p$; for $k=0$ use the base state with positions $2,3$ absent. Its endpoint residue modulo $h$ is $(2k+1)cp$, because all the other endpoint coefficients vanish there. On the next even diagonal, of length $8k+10$, the only double $h$ pole at first position $3$ is the product of the two incoming shears of the previous endpoint. The first sign is positive and the second is $(-1)^{(8k+4)/4}=-1$. Mixed incoming terms have only a single pole. Therefore the numerator $up$ of $z_3=up/h^2+vp/h$ is the negative of that endpoint residue, and $u=-(2k+1)c$.

**Odd to even: the simple poles.** On this even diagonal, the ordinary components at first positions $0,1,2$ equal their integral raw components: an incoming first shear lands only at position $3$, and a backward adjacent pair has first position at least $3$ by the weight equation. In the component at position $2$, $H_{3,1}$ is divisible by $h$, so there is no double pole; the rational-state bounds force $z_2=C/h$. Cancellation of its simple pole gives $C=4(k+1)u$. Similarly $H_{3,2}$ and $H_{3,3}$ are divisible by $h$, forcing $z_1=Bp/h$ and $z_0=A/h$. The endpoint pole equation modulo $h$ is $A-C+(2B+C)q^2=0$, by step 5.1. The elements $1,q^2$ are rationally independent in that residue field, so $A=C$ and $B=-C/2$. This proves $z_2=z_0=C/h$, $z_1=-Cp/(2h)$, with $C=-4(k+1)(2k+1)c$; no value of $v$ is needed. Its endpoint modulo $p$ is $-(2k+3)C$, since the odd-position states vanish there and $H_{2,2}=4k+5$ for length $8k+10$.

**Even to odd: the two double poles.** Let the preceding even diagonal have length $8k+2$, with the state just proved and scalar $C$, and consider the next odd diagonal of length $m=8k+4$, with $k\ge1$. At first position $3$, the double $p$ pole comes only from both shears of the preceding raw vector at position $2$. Its two signs are negative and positive. That raw coefficient evaluated modulo $p$ is $C/h=-C/2$: its ordinary component is integral by step 8.1, and the $z_3$ contribution vanishes because it has a factor $p$. Thus $c_3=C/2=:c'$. At first position $1$, the double pole comes from both shears of the preceding endpoint, again with negative total sign. That endpoint equals $-(2k+1)C$ modulo $p$. On the current diagonal its double-pole numerator is $c_1+(4k+1)c'$, using $H_{3,2}=4k+1$. Equating it to $(2k+1)C=(4k+2)c'$ forces $c_1=c'$. Single-pole mixed terms cannot alter either double-pole equation.

**Even to odd: the simple poles.** The ordinary component at first position $2$ is integral. An incoming first shear lands at positions $1,3$; an incoming second shear would have to start in the backward mixed pair at second position $m-3$, which is odd and is therefore killed by the even link. Hence $z_2+c'H_{3,1}/p^2$ has no pole, giving $A_2=(4k+1)c'$. The ordinary endpoint is also integral: no first shear lands at position $0$, and the backward mixed pair requires first position at least $1$. Its pole equation is $A_0-(4k+2)c'+(4k+2)A_2-(4k+2)(4k+1)c'=0$, so $A_0=(4k+2)c'$. Consequently the odd state has exactly the form used in step 7.1. Combining steps 8.1 and 9.1 gives the recurrence $c_{k+1}=-(2k+2)(2k+1)c_k$, and therefore $c_k=(-1)^{k+1}(2k)!$.

**Nonzero endpoint residues in every cut.** The odd endpoint residue is $(2k+1)c_kp=(-1)^k(2k+1)!(q^3-q)$ modulo $h$. The following even scalar is $C=(-1)^k2(2k+2)!$, and its endpoint residue is $-(2k+3)C=(-1)^{k+1}2(2k+3)!$ modulo $p$. Multiplication by powers of $q$ identifies these ideals with $(q^4+1)$ and $(q^2+1)$ respectively. These residues are nonzero in their characteristic-zero residue fields, so every asserted endpoint coefficient is nonzero. The computation used only incoming shears and thus applies to every containing finite cut; step 1.1 also gives their coherence. Finite arithmetic, explicit projections and finite induction used no choice. This proves the stated escape of normalized corrected lifts.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.1 checks zero correction errors and finite termination; step 2.1 checks all vanishing endpoints.
Step 6.1 proves the first cut directly with positions 2 and 3 excluded.
Steps 7.1 through 11.1 prove all nonzero endpoint residues, including every cut boundary.
Only finite induction, explicit sums and uniquely determined scalar extraction are used.
